subject: Hospitality
title: Cross-Cultural Service Training
description: A 60-second lesson on Cross-Cultural Service Training.

hook.text: A thumbs-up is positive in America but offensive in parts of the Middle East. Cross-cultural training prevents disasters.

buildup.text: Hotels serving international guests train staff on greeting customs, dining etiquette, religious practices.

discovery.text: Chinese guests value specific room numbers (8 is lucky, 4 is unlucky). Japanese guests expect slippers and robes.

twist.text: Over-stereotyping backfires. Assuming all Asian guests want chopsticks or all Middle Eastern guests avoid alcohol offends too.

climax.text: The best training teaches cultural awareness without stereotyping—observe, ask, and adapt to each individual guest.

punchline.text: Observe, don't assume. Great service respects both the culture and the individual.

quiz.question: What is the main risk of cross-cultural service training?
options: Over-stereotyping—assuming all guests from one culture have the same preferences
